alternatives.label: Molecular disease, human health and treatment
alternatives.concept: A biomedical-science programme progressing from molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, anatomy and physiology to genetics, disease, infection, pharmacology, laboratory investigation and population and patient health. Introductory physical and chemical modelling and experiments support these foundations. It responds to the medically oriented MWT core while differing from its sustained organic chemistry, biomaterials, mechanobiology and engineering-project formation.

alternatives.label: Biomedical science, data & imaging methods
alternatives.concept: A biomedical-science programme joining molecular, physiological and disease inquiry and laboratory work to programming, mathematical models, statistical learning and image-processing methods. Introductory physical and chemical foundations support the biological systems. The computational courses supply methods relevant to biomedical research; they do not guarantee clinical-image training, diagnostic qualification or TU/e’s full engineering laboratories.

alternatives.distinctness: Five courses37.5EC differ in each direction. The first develops epidemiology, infection/immunity, neurobiology, perception/action and patient-health psychology; the second develops programming, linear algebra, numerical methods, image processing and neural networks. Shared biomedical laboratory/disease and introductory physical foundations support coherent but different research priorities.

candidates.label: Regenerative medicine, biomaterials and medical-technology design
candidates.reason: UCR has strong molecular and biomedical sciences and one life-science laboratory, but no biomaterials, tissue engineering, regenerative-medicine laboratory, biofabrication or medical-device-design sequence from which to build a separate 24-course programme without padding it with merely adjacent biology or data courses.

selection.assessment: Two related biomedical-science responses retained after actual content review and stronger physical/chemical foundations. The second changes five courses37.5EC toward data/modelling/imaging methods. A separate regenerative/material/device direction cannot be sustained: actual cell repair/genetics/biopolymer experiments are genuine contributions but do not establish the missing tissue-engineering, fabrication and medical-device project sequence. No degree-title-only rejection; no forced third.

routeSelection.basis: Exact target-named MWT specialization, confirmed by current PER Appendix2; alternative BBT core not imported. Generation2026 chart follows current formal course codes.

notes.text: TU/e MWT joins medical and life sciences to organic chemistry, physics, mechanobiology, materials, biological-system modelling and staged engineering projects. UCR offers molecular and cellular biology, human physiology and disease, laboratory methods, introductory physical and chemical experiments and quantitative study. The data option adds computational imaging methods. Neither reproduces the full specialist engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. The UCR computational courses do not guarantee clinical datasets or clinical training.

trace: introduces data collection, cleaning, analysis and visualisation for biomedical evidence
Actual regression/classification/model validation on real data supports quantitative biomedical inquiry as transferable methods; no compulsory biomedical-data application assumed.
Actual image filtering/segmentation/features and Python/OpenCV recognition-pipeline evaluation supply imaging methods; the evidence does not require clinical images or medical acquisition physics.
Actual neural-network learning/evaluation with image/time-series/text applications supplies computational pattern methods; no compulsory biomedical dataset assumed.

audience.programmeDescription: TU/e Medical Sciences and Engineering studies molecular and cellular processes in health and disease and uses technology to investigate biomedical problems. Its MWT core combines biological and chemical science with mathematics, physics, laboratory skills and engineering projects.
audience.comparisonExplanation: TU/e MWT joins medical and life sciences to organic chemistry, physics, mechanobiology, materials, biological-system modelling and staged engineering projects. UCR offers molecular and cellular biology, human physiology and disease, laboratory methods, introductory physical and chemical experiments and quantitative study. The data option adds computational imaging methods. Neither reproduces the full specialist engineering laboratories or compulsory biomedical final project. The UCR computational courses do not guarantee clinical datasets or clinical training.
